views.signature: void Original_pop_view_merge(void * savedView, void * currentView, void * resultView)

observations: If result != current, first assign whole current view into result.

For nonnull saved with all three identities distinct, assign whole current view into result again; then assign saved viewport only. This is two current assignments plus saved viewport assignment, not a single copied saved view.
Use saved TargetPoint getter, which may repair its stale mirror, then result SetTargetPoint; scalar failure/mirror rules remain source-defined.

Saved name copied only if its trimmed temporary is nonempty, equals original untrimmed saved name, and current/result viewType !=1. Exact native trim/compare semantics must be inspected before using managed string operations.
Call SetScreenPort(result,0,0,0,0,0,0) after merge; actual primitive failure/mutation semantics must be verified.
Pop then SetView/client-screen restores, removes last, sets cursor=count-1 and returnsfalse. Full caller/document/window effects remain unfinished.
limits: Static original analysis only; no original runtime execution.
No guessed name trimming, screen setter, SetView or document effect is implemented from this preliminary merge map.
Managed pointer identity/alias guards require explicit tests; native freed-pointer behavior is not an iOS API.
